THE PLAN AT A GLANCE

Required at your target retirement age

How this calculation works

Yearly cash flows occur at the beginning of each year, followed by growth. Contributions increase annually until retirement. Expenses and pension rise with inflation. Each goal grows at its own inflation rate (your plan rate unless you set one) and is withdrawn from this same portfolio at its scheduled age; money coming in is added the same way. Retirement income streams reduce spending while they last, rising with inflation unless marked fixed. Tax on withdrawals is the share of each withdrawal lost to tax: at 20%, covering ₹80 of spending or goals means withdrawing ₹100. Money coming in is treated as already taxed.

Returns are effective annual nominal assumptions. No taxes, fees, or random market returns are modeled. The forecast finds the earliest whole age that funds the plan through the selected horizon.

These are scenarios, not guarantees or investment recommendations.

Your investments, holding by holding

Split your retirement investments into holdings. Their total becomes your retirement investments figure.

The milestones along your way.

Big expenses and money coming in both flow through your retirement portfolio. Enter each amount in today’s money. It grows at its own inflation rate until the year it happens.

Leave blank to use your plan’s rate. Education and healthcare often rise faster than general inflation. Use 0% for an amount that won’t grow, such as a fixed bonus.

The effect on your freedom

These items use the same savings pool as your retirement, so they are never counted as extra assets.

Income during retirement.

Rent, an annuity, EPF or a spouse’s pension reduce what your portfolio has to pay each year. Enter amounts in today’s money.

Stress settings

How much returns swing from year to year: roughly 15–18% for all equity, 8–12% for a balanced mix, 3–5% for mostly debt.

TIMING MATTERS
How the stress test works

Each simulated future draws a fresh return for every year: your assumed return (before or after retirement) plus a random swing sized by volatility, following a bell curve and floored at −90%. Everything else — contributions, spending, goals, income and tax — follows your plan exactly.

A future succeeds if the portfolio never runs short before your planning age. Because gains and losses compound unevenly, the typical outcome is usually below the steady-returns line even though average returns match your assumption.

Results are repeatable for the same plan; “New random futures” draws a different set. This is a model of uncertainty, not a forecast or advice.
